title: Reject Windows junction aliases in replay input paths
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

A Windows directory junction can pass `symlink_free_relative_path` because its mode is a directory, not a symbolic link. A package then reads changed bytes through `alias/dep.json`, while a real Git change to `src/dep.json` produces an empty replay matrix and `count=0`.

This tooling fix checks the junction's `IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT` in the existing `lstat` result and rejects it before descendant lookup, metadata acceptance or planning. It preserves regular/deleted-input selection, existing symbolic-link controls and a junction at the repository root. Four files change: the guard, behavioral tests, the package guide and a [source-bound evidence note](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4bd03cdf83b6c5ec75b787bdec6cd9c5d225e36b/docs/research/replay-input-junctions.md). No scientific artifacts, frozen pins or selected result change.

## Task and overlap

- Base: current canonical main `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, refreshed unchanged before publication; contribution head `4bd03cdf83b6c5ec75b787bdec6cd9c5d225e36b`.
- Task `portable-replay`, priority revision 7; chooser nonce `59d790bcbb44891de2b3ea502e8df5eb`. Scope **changed** from container comparison to a platform-specific dependency boundary because it can silently omit required verification. Handoffs were checked before the picker.
- [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2983#discussioncomment-19152881).
- Nearest predecessor: #2986 explicitly excluded Windows reparse points. #3007 covers exact Git spelling; #4730 concerns temporary-root aliases. This closes the distinct directory-junction input boundary.
- Final overlap: 306 open PR bodies at 19:14 UTC, 4,638 Discussion records at 19:15 UTC, complete pagination, and all 7,267 tracked local README/TASK/ledger records. Targeted all-state PR searches also checked junction/reparse references. No same-scope repair appeared; arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain outside coverage.

## Validation

Native Windows 11 build 26300, CPython 3.12.0, Git 2.47.1.windows.1.

```sh
python -B tests/test_research_symlink_inputs.py
python -O -B tests/test_research_symlink_inputs.py
```

Each runs 14 tests: 13 pass and the existing POSIX-permission test skips. **All four new native junction groups execute.** A platform-neutral tag/lookup control also runs. The native tests use actual junctions, committed input spellings and a real target-only Git commit. Rejection leaves stdout empty and an existing workflow-output file unchanged; the canonical input then selects its consumer.

The same five added groups against the authenticated original runner give four failures and one root-junction positive pass. The original actual-Git CLI returns exit 0, `{"include": []}` and `count=0`; the fixed CLI rejects the junction.

Additional unchanged modules:

| Command suffix after `python -B tests/` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test_research_input_paths.py` | 5 pass |
| `test_research_head_pin_paths.py` | 1 pass, 2 platform skips |
| `test_research_replay_selection.py` | 8 pass, 1 platform skip |
| `test_research_sparse_planning.py` | 11 pass |
| `test_research_commit_bytes.py` | 11 pass |
| `test_research_git_spelling.py` with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` | 8 pass, 1 platform skip |

The existing Git-spelling Unicode diagnostic assertion fails under default CP1252 on **both baseline and patched code**, matching the [previously reported fixture issue](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2983#discussioncomment-18981956). It passes with the explicit UTF-8 protocol and is unchanged here. Replay-selection tests initially lacked their sparse-omitted workflow file; after materializing it unchanged, they pass.

Selected source/metadata orientation passes before and after; all four working files equal their committed bytes; `git diff --check` passes. No selected cold replay, repository-wide historical replay or independent human review is claimed. The shared-runner change selects all registered packages under existing CI policy; frozen historical pins were not rewritten. Hosted results are separate from these local checks.

## Credit

Prepared for Mihir Srivastava with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Retains Nick Petalas's PR2986 and test lineage, EdDiboi's earlier alias finding, woklerx's lexical guard, Charles Bethin's replay-selection work, Douglas Colkitt's runner and the retained contributors. The original runner's exact Git blob and SHA256 are in the evidence note.

## Open next questions

Native junction behavior requires Windows; other hosts retain the platform-neutral tag and POSIX alias controls. The checkout must remain stable. Hard links, other reparse-point families, concurrent writers and transitive dependency discovery are outside this patch. Broader alias work needs a separate concrete failure and contract; no new mathematical question or kappa claim follows.
